clue.text: Abscond with the stakes in Powys

parts.note: to welsh is to run off without paying a debt, especially a bet
a pool is the total money staked by gamblers

explanation.surface: Someone runs off with the betting money somewhere in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Powys is a county in mid-Wales; the definition is the phrase 'in Powys', standing for a town found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Welshpool is a market town in the Welsh county of Powys.

clue.text: Does some spotting in the Mersey estuary

indicators.note: the word in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across the join

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers are out looking at the mouth of the Mersey.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'MersEY ESTuary'; the Mersey is the river that flows out past Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch or look at it, so this verb form matches looking out for things.

clue.text: It may dawn on one getting up early

definitions.text: It may dawn on one getting up early

parts.words: It may dawn on one getting up early
parts.note: read literally, it is the morning event an early riser sees as day breaks; 'dawn on' pretends to mean realise

explanation.surface: An early riser suddenly realises something.
explanation.definitionFit: The appearance of the sun at daybreak is what an early riser witnesses.

clue.text: A clue for this is a difficult matter

definitions.text: A clue for this is a difficult matter

parts.words: A clue for this is a difficult matter
parts.note: a crossword clue is itself a puzzle to be solved, and the word also means any tricky situation

explanation.surface: Writing a clue for this word is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle set for solving and a troublesome situation are both senses of the same word.

clue.text: Savoury dish served in the Tivoli once

indicators.note: food served in a place is contained within it, so the letters are inside the following words

explanation.surface: A tasty dish that used to be on the menu at the Tivoli.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles 'TivOLI Once'; the Tivoli is a pleasure garden in Copenhagen, also a name used for restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: An olio is a spicy stew of meat and vegetables, a savoury Spanish dish.

clue.text: Disposal of lots of goods at knock-down prices

definitions.text: Disposal of lots of goods at knock-down prices

parts.words: Disposal of lots of goods at knock-down prices
parts.note: lots are numbered items at auction and knock-down refers to the hammer falling, not cheap bargains

explanation.surface: A clearance sale of plenty of stock at very cheap prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots are sold one by one, each price settled when the auctioneer's hammer falls.

clue.text: Boost for worried ten men without pluck

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters wrap round the other piece
worried here means agitated or troubled, so the letters of ten men are stirred up

parts.note: pluck means bravery, courage

explanation.surface: A morale boost for ten anxious men lacking nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' turns TEN MEN into EN...MENT, and 'without' (meaning outside) puts it around COURAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Encouragement is support that gives someone heart, a lift in confidence.

clue.text: Stuff to make a philosopher weep?

definitions.text: Stuff to make a philosopher weep?

parts.words: Stuff to make a philosopher weep?
parts.note: stuff is the stuffing for poultry; a wise thinker is a sage, and the vegetable that brings tears is the onion

explanation.surface: Something that would bring a wise thinker to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a vague noun but means stuffing for a roast; the wise man's tears come from the onions beside him.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic British stuffing made with the herb and chopped bulbs, served with roast chicken.

clue.text: Headed by a retiring few, they're generally drunk

definitions.text: Headed by a retiring few, they're generally drunk

parts.words: Headed by a retiring few, they're generally drunk
parts.note: the drinks are taken by people retiring to bed, and they head the night; drunk means consumed, not intoxicated

explanation.surface: A small group of shy leaders who are usually inebriated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' suggests shy people and 'drunk' suggests tipsy ones, but they are bedtime drinkers and drinks that are swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is an alcoholic drink taken just before going to bed.

clue.text: One doesn't run after it, presumably

definitions.text: One doesn't run after it, presumably

parts.words: One doesn't run after it, presumably
parts.note: no service runs after it on the timetable, though it reads as if no one chases it

explanation.surface: Something nobody bothers to chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run after' suggests chasing; it means no train runs later that night.
explanation.definitionFit: The final departure of the day on a railway line has nothing scheduled after it.

clue.text: One Latin law of a prickly kind

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
lex is the Latin word for law

explanation.surface: A single Latin statute of a particularly thorny sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the botanical genus of holly, a spiny-leaved shrub.

clue.text: Take a bow for playing a Shakespearean unisex character

definitions.meaning: this stringed instrument is played with a bow
the heroine of Twelfth Night, who disguises herself as a young man, Cesario

explanation.surface: An actor in a cross-dressing Shakespeare role takes a bow after the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an instrument a little larger than a violin and the cross-dressed heroine of Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Explosive star giving the thumbs down to Virginia

parts.note: a thumbs down is a refusal, a no
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A celebrity rejects the state of Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly flares up in brightness through a thermonuclear outburst.

clue.text: Beat into a soft plastic mass

definitions.meaning: a moist, malleable substance such as dough or glue

explanation.definitionFit: Both a slang word for thrashing someone and a smooth, malleable substance.

clue.text: Pictures changing wives

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the word that follows swap places

explanation.surface: Photographs of men swapping spouses.
explanation.definitionFit: Views are scenes or images, as on picture postcards.

clue.text: Old boat on a stretch of water in the Wirral

parts.note: a hoy is an old type of small coastal sailing vessel
a lake is an inland body of water

explanation.surface: An antique vessel sitting on a lake on Merseyside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wirral is a peninsula near Liverpool; the definition is 'in the Wirral', standing for a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoylake is a seaside town on the north coast of the Wirral peninsula.

clue.text: Sort of ragtime novel sleuth

indicators.note: to sort something is to rearrange it, so the letters of ragtime are reordered

explanation.surface: A kind of ragtime music from a detective story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like 'new' but means a detective from fiction: Georges Simenon's French police inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Maigret is the fictional Paris detective in Georges Simenon's books.

clue.text: Bar foreign nobleman taking precedence over the Queen

indicators.note: going in front of, so the first piece is written before the second

parts.note: a count is a continental nobleman, matching the British earl
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A European aristocrat goes ahead of the monarch in matters of protocol.
explanation.definitionFit: A counter is the long surface in a pub or shop across which customers are served.

clue.text: Appreciate how to make money

definitions.meaning: to grasp or understand something fully
to convert assets into cash or gain a sum by selling

explanation.surface: Learning how to earn money.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both coming to understand and turning property into cash.

clue.text: Elderly lady party to a flutter?

parts.note: a do is an informal party
a flutter is a small bet, a wager

explanation.surface: An old lady takes part in a small bet.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is British slang for a small bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title from her late husband, typically a dignified older woman.

clue.text: Hopelessness oddly praised

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters of praised come out in a strange order

explanation.surface: Feeling despondent after being praised in a peculiar way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' could suggest taking odd letters, but those give PASD; here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the complete loss of hope.

clue.text: Soft! Goddess of mischief is after crown

indicators.note: the goddess is placed after the first piece, so her name follows it

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Quiet! The goddess of mischief wants the royal crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crown' is the top of the head, not a monarch's headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: The pate is the top of the head, also called the crown.

clue.text: Deep voice has a fishy ring

parts.note: the bass is a fish, so fishy points to that fish
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A low singing voice with a suspicious tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Basso is the Italian term for a bass singer or the lowest male voice.

clue.text: Native warriors guarding a parliamentarian, one on each side

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding to protect, so these letters enclose the politician
a letter placed on each side means it appears twice, once at each end

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Tribal fighters protecting a Member of Parliament, one posted on either flank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on each side' doubles I, and 'guarding' puts the pair round MP.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a body of Zulu warriors.

clue.text: An afterthought put on east end of church?

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: An addition tacked on to the eastern part of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: An apse is traditionally at the east end of a church, which is why 'east' fits the surface so well.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the rounded recess at the far end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Slip of the lips, so to speak

definitions.text: Slip of the lips, so to speak

parts.words: Slip of the lips, so to speak
parts.note: a speech defect is a slip the lips make; both slip and lips use the same four letters as it

explanation.surface: A mistake made when speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A lisp is a speech defect turning s sounds into th sounds.

clue.text: No politics, Mac; they could be so involved

definitions.text: No politics, Mac; they could be so involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Advice to a Scot to avoid politics because it gets too tangled.
explanation.walkthrough: Mac is a casual address to a man, particularly a Scot; the whole clue also says politics brings these tangles.
explanation.definitionFit: Complications are tangled difficulties, just what involvement in politics brings.

clue.text: Signal of great help in a way

indicators.note: in a way here suggests the letters are put into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A signal that proves very helpful.
explanation.definitionFit: To telegraph is to signal something, as by wire or by an obvious gesture.
